target_customer: Sneaker and streetwear shoppers paying for membership
problem: Hyped sneakers and streetwear sell out in minutes, so buyers needed instant restock and release alerts and fast checkout.
business_model: Paid membership of about 25 to 36 dollars per year per TechCrunch
product_category: consumer shopping app, release and restock alerts

founders.name: Luke Miles
founders.background_notes: Sole founder on the YC page. TechCrunch says he wrote code that emailed him when sold-out Supreme items returned, then added texts, charged for it and built an app.

competitors.name: GOAT
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as a sneaker app

competitors.name: Nike SNKRS
competitors.traction_then: TechCrunch calls it a possible future competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: Scraping stores for stock changes and auto-filling checkout is modest engineering but brittle against site changes.

defensibility.rationale: Alerts were easy to copy, retailers could block bots, and Nike and Adidas were launching their own apps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Retailer apps and drop systems grew in 2016 and 2017. No acquisition of Restocks was found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch describes strong demand for limited streetwear and sneaker drops and a reviewer who bought more through the app than any mobile commerce app other than Amazon.

branding.domain_note: Listed domain restocks.io returned 404; the name was later used by an unrelated Belgian resale business (Restocks BV).

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch coverage in 2016 but a generic name that collides with later unrelated businesses and Shopify restock apps.

outcome_analysis: Restocks started from a founder's own Supreme restock script and showed real purchase activity in a TechCrunch review, but no funding, traction numbers or shutdown story is public. The cause of inactivity is not public, so failure factors stay empty. Retailer drop apps and resale marketplaces were converging on the same customers.
notes: YC page says funded by Y Combinator and angel investors without amounts. Website restocks.io returned 404. The App Store app called Restocks belongs to Restocks BV, a different company. Cause of inactivity not public.
